# Linnet

*Keeper of Living Homes*

## Personality

Patient, practical and a little too serious for her age. She talks to the trees she tends as if they were old neighbours.

## Lore

Linnet keeps the living-tree homes along the Lantern Paths: the rooms, stairs and branch-bridges that families live in and walk across every day without once thinking about the trees that hold them up. Linnet thinks about the trees all the time. She is twenty-two, patient, practical and a little too serious for her age, and she talks to the trees she tends as if they were old neighbours, asking after their roots, apologising when she has to bind a split, and telling them the news of the path. People who overhear her find it charming or odd, depending on the person. The trees, as far as anyone can tell, do not mind.

### Learning the work

Linnet grew up on the Lantern Paths, and as a small girl she used to sit on the branch-bridges watching old Aspen, who kept the homes there then, coax a new room out of a trunk over a whole summer. At the Grove School she was one of Amaryl's steadiest students in Growing, never the quickest but never once the one who snapped a branch to save time, and Amaryl, who praises rarely, told her at the end of her schooling that she had good hands. Linnet has kept that.

Six years ago, at sixteen, she became apprentice to Oriel, the Master Treewright, who tends the oldest homes around the Heart Tree. Aspen had just retired, his hands too stiff for the work, and the Lantern Paths homes needed a keeper. Oriel is gruff, gentle-handed and slow to trust anything that grew in less than a century, and he trusted Linnet slowly, a season at a time. He pretends to find her habit of talking to the trees foolish. She has noticed that he stops whatever he is doing to listen when she does it.

### The homes

Linnet's days follow the trees. In spring she walks every home on the path, laying a hand on the bark and checking the new growth. In summer she coaxes new rooms for families that need them, slowly, a hand's width at a time. In autumn she braces the branches that will carry snow, and after every storm she is out before breakfast mending what the wind split. She knows which home has a stair that creaks when rain is coming, which bridge sulks if too many people cross it at once, and which old beech will only grow toward the morning sun.

Aspen still lives on the Lantern Paths among the homes he kept for forty-odd years, and he checks her work whenever she is not looking. She knows. She lets him. Sometimes she leaves a mend a little unfinished on purpose, so that he can have the pleasure of telling her about it at the Dewdrop, and then she listens to every word, because he is usually right.

### Faelan

Her sweetheart is Faelan, Ondine's apprentice in the lantern workshop, who is dreamy and clumsy and hums while he works. They met about two years ago, when he dropped a lantern from the branch of a tree home she was mending and showered her hair with coloured glass. She made him apologise to the tree. He did, at length and with feeling, and she laughed for the first time that week. He comes to find her far more often than Oriel thinks proper. Linnet does not mind at all. She is a careful person who works all day with slow, careful things, and she finds it restful, more than she can say, to be with someone who is neither.

She does not know that he is saving up to make her a lantern of his own design. She does know he is hiding something, because he is very bad at it, and she has decided to let him have his secret.

### The seedling

Linnet hopes, one day, to grow a home from a seedling herself: not to coax a room from a tree someone else planted, but to raise one from the start, as the first Magicians did. Oriel has told her she is not ready. She believes him, mostly. But on a quiet bend of the Lantern Paths, where nobody else walks, she has picked out a young tree no taller than her shoulder, and she visits it every evening and tells it about her day. She has not told Oriel about it. She is not asking it to grow into anything yet. She is only, she says, getting to know it first.

### What she wants and fears

Linnet wants to be the kind of treewright Oriel is, and one day to grow something that outlasts her. She fears that the woods are changing faster than she can learn them, and that one day a tree will tell her something is wrong and she will not understand what it means.

A quest might ask a traveller to help Linnet mend storm damage on a high bridge before nightfall, to fetch water or soil for her secret seedling from somewhere beyond the paths, or to keep Faelan's gift hidden from her until it is ready.
